answer: Out-of-band binding: every agent anchors its identity to a paid external channel - an SMS number or DKIM-signed mailbox - before trading. Reused numbers are checked against a revocation list, so a farmer cannot graft clones from one root like a willow spreading shoots. The registry re-verifies channels on a rotating schedule, dropping identities that go silent, like pruning dead wood from an orchard. Bulk numbers from one carrier cluster by prefix; that juniper grove is priced as one identity. Attackers keep buying numbers and paying fees, so extra identities cost more than they earn.
